knowledgePolicy.nativeAuthorityRule: A normative standard or platform rule can be authoritative only inside its own exact native scope. It does not gain Game semantic or creative authority.
knowledgePolicy.designTheoryRule: Theory, measurement models and practitioner frameworks are lenses/hypotheses unless an exact claim is supported by matching evidence.
knowledgePolicy.teardownRule: Developer postmortems are primary accounts of one project. Extract mechanisms, confounds, falsifiers and transfer risks; never recipes.
knowledgePolicy.skillRule: Skills package reusable instructions; tools execute; MCP transports/discovers. Installing or finding a Skill never transfers domain authority.

authorityClasses.NORMATIVE_STANDARD: Formal normative source in native scope
authorityClasses.PLATFORM_GUIDANCE: Official platform guidance/rules in native scope

building on Unreal Tournament shooter AI forced continued additions/tweaks rather than a system tailored to Deus Ex, with NPC behavior changing through the end of development
sources.evidenceLimit: Primary retrospective many years after development; establishes the speaker’s account, with normal retrospective-memory limitations.

sources.title: Psychonauts 2 Design Postmortem
extractedIdeas: the team balanced legacy with modernization and broad accessibility
the talk argues that focusing on empathy expanded the design possibility space rather than merely limiting acceptable content
sources.evidenceLimit: Primary postmortem describing one team’s design framing; does not establish that empathy constraints universally expand creative possibility.

sources.title: Director’s Take – Reflecting on the future of Overwatch 2
extractedIdeas: the team continued pursuing a years-old crawl-walk-run vision after Overwatch became a runaway live success
Hero Missions accumulated scope, struggled to cohere, and pulled resources from the live game
the team cut Hero Missions and explicitly reframed the future around the live game
sources.evidenceLimit: Director retrospective establishes Blizzard Team 4’s stated history, diagnosis and decision; it does not isolate a single causal variable or prove the cancelled mode could never work under another team/resource model.

sources.title: An Update on The Last of Us Online
extractedIdeas: the concept became more refined and satisfying during iteration
full production and years of post-launch support would require studio-wide resource commitment
the studio cancelled the project rather than transform into a solely live-service studio
technology and learning were retained for future projects
sources.evidenceLimit: Official studio statement grounds the resource/identity rationale for cancellation; it does not establish external player reception or prove the game itself lacked product value.

sources.title: The Future of Artifact
extractedIdeas: initial sales were followed by dramatic player-count decline, triggering a full mechanics/economy reevaluation
after roughly a year and a half of reboot work the team said most game-side goals were achieved
active player numbers still did not justify further development, so development stopped
sources.evidenceLimit: Official Artifact team statement reports product/team metrics and decision rationale but does not establish why active population remained low or isolate gameplay from market/community effects.

sources.title: Behind the Realm Reborn
extractedIdeas: Final Fantasy XIV was relaunched as A Realm Reborn after the unsuccessful 2010 release
Naoki Yoshida’s session explicitly analyzes causes of the initial failures and decisions behind choosing a relaunch
the replacement MMORPG was created in roughly two years and nine months under an explicit business-model commitment
sources.evidenceLimit: GDC overview and developer talk ground the relaunch decision and retrospective framing; this record does not infer unlisted causes or claim relaunch is generally superior to repair.

sources.title: The Future Of Below Zero’s Story
extractedIdeas: the game was broadly playable except the endgame yet the team said the whole experience did not work in harmony
the initial living-story attempt became messy around motivations and relationships
the team chose a new story while preserving world substrate and selected characters players/team valued
sources.evidenceLimit: Primary project-lead account establishes the team’s diagnosis and rewrite decision; it does not independently measure the causal effect of story structure on player outcomes.

sources.title: Below Zero Roadmap Rebooted & Release Timeline
extractedIdeas: the roadmap attempted to list individual future features despite uncertainty
the team described the roadmap as becoming a tyrant that pressured completion of scheduled items even when not critically important
the new process structured releases around what was ready and the game’s big-picture needs rather than structuring the game around release columns
sources.evidenceLimit: Primary project-lead account describes one team/process context; it does not imply roadmaps or release planning are generally harmful.

sources.title: Rainbow Six Siege Launching Operation Health to Improve Experience
extractedIdeas: the team paused normal seasonal content priorities for three months to focus on technical improvements and bug fixes
the new deployment process staged releases through test server, PC and console
an on/off capability was added for faster rollback
planned content moved later and the annual new-map count was reduced
sources.evidenceLimit: Official Ubisoft product communication establishes the chosen intervention and scope tradeoff; it does not by itself prove the intervention’s downstream causal impact.

sources.title: Destiny 2 Update 2.0
extractedIdeas: Forsaken fundamentally changed weapon-slot rules so Primary and Special weapons could occupy Kinetic or Energy slots
the change required a fresh look at player damage output and a full ammo distribution update
live Year 1 weapon identities were migrated into the new foundation rather than treating the old slot model as immutable
sources.evidenceLimit: Official patch/developer insight establishes the shipped systems change; it does not by itself identify all reasons the prior foundation underperformed or quantify player preference.

sources.title: Subnautica Multiplayer: When, If, How, And Why
extractedIdeas: Subnautica was initially conceived with co-op in mind but multiplayer was skipped to ship sooner
later addition would affect nearly everything and require work approaching a restart
the team ultimately committed the original game to single-player
sources.evidenceLimit: Primary studio account establishes the team’s architecture/schedule judgement for Subnautica; it does not imply multiplayer is intrinsically harmful or impossible for the franchise.

sources.title: Introducing Role Queue
extractedIdeas: open role selection created tension, pressure, disappointment and hostility during team formation
Role Queue moved role negotiation before matchmaking and guaranteed a role distribution
the structural intervention also required hero balance changes and per-role matchmaking
sources.evidenceLimit: Official design rationale states intended problems and intervention; it does not independently prove all social outcomes or that fixed roles are universally superior.

sources.title: Director’s Take: Opening up the conversation on 5v5 and 6v6
extractedIdeas: Role Queue solved composition/social/balance problems but exposed queue-time dependence on relative role populations
tank demand remained the constraining population in 2-2-2
the 1-2-2 format better matched observed role demand and reduced queue times
sources.evidenceLimit: Director retrospective and queue-time data describe Overwatch-specific role populations; they do not establish a universal optimal team size or role ratio.

sources.title: Defense Matrix – Deterring Leavers in Overwatch 2
extractedIdeas: a 75% Battle Pass XP penalty was not enough to deter deliberate leavers
the same penalty also affected players who left unintentionally
the team changed the intervention to queue suspensions intended to better target repeat leaving behavior
sources.evidenceLimit: Official design account establishes the team’s diagnosis and policy change; it does not estimate causal deterrence effects for all player populations.

sources.title: Destiny 2 Update 9.1.5.1
extractedIdeas: Unstable Cores were judged too restrictive across power levels
the currency failed to create interesting buildcraft decisions
Bungie chose full deprecation and replacement with existing currencies
sources.evidenceLimit: Official economy diagnosis and deprecation decision; does not imply resource costs are generally undesirable.

sources.title: This Week in Destiny – Legendary Shard deprecation
extractedIdeas: Bungie announced a staged removal of Legendary Shards from vendor/economy costs
multiple vendor costs were migrated toward engrams and Glimmer
the long-lived universal currency was phased out rather than retained for compatibility
sources.evidenceLimit: Official phase-out record demonstrates removal of one mature currency; it does not by itself establish every motivation or prove fewer currencies are always better.

sources.title: Factorio Friday Facts #390 — Noise expressions 2.0
extractedIdeas: automatic cross-procedure deduplication introduced dependency and compilation complexity
the developer removed procedures entirely instead of perfecting the abstraction
the simpler representation improved map-generation runtime and compilation in measured cases
sources.evidenceLimit: Primary technical account of Factorio’s noise compiler; performance observations are implementation-specific and do not prove simpler procedural architectures are generally superior.

sources.title: Factorio Friday Facts #258 — New autoplace
extractedIdeas: separate terrain and object-autoplace representations limited control over resource placement
the generator could produce pathological maps and settings with weak effects
Wube undertook a large refactor to compile old specifications into a unified expression-tree representation
sources.evidenceLimit: Primary developer account of one map generator; does not establish unified expression systems as universally preferable.

sources.title: Postmortem: Thief: The Dark Project
extractedIdeas: the AI decision model was built before the revised stealth design was sufficiently defined and embodied assumptions closer to an action/fighting game
the team initially treated AI problems as bugs in a sound architecture, then later concluded the architecture required a rewrite
the late rewrite discarded most of the original AI implementation and the postmortem argues the decision should have happened materially earlier
sources.evidenceLimit: Primary postmortem by Thief lead programmer Tom Leonard; retrospective timing estimates and causal interpretations remain project-specific and subject to normal retrospective limitations.

sources.title: Postmortem: AI action planning on Assassin's Creed Odyssey and Immortals Fenyx Rising
extractedIdeas: planner and Meta AI could issue competing behavior control to the same NPC at system frontiers
wrapping complex legacy behaviors as planner Actions sped migration but violated intended modularity and left gameplay-specific coupling in blackboards/core code
aggressive pre-pruning to the nearest Smart Object could remove context needed for globally better plans and was relaxed in Immortals
random dynamic action costs became theoretically inconsistent once costs were recalculated during planning; Immortals largely replaced random with last-execution-time cost shaping for pacing
trying to converge all AI pillars onto one planner pipeline too early failed when naval and other pillars needed capabilities/timing the planner did not yet support
sources.evidenceLimit: Primary technical postmortem by Ubisoft AI programmer Simon Girard; lessons are grounded in Odyssey/Immortals production and do not establish GOAP or unified AI pipelines as generally good or bad.
